nate: Heads-up — CI perf alert after last week's infra merge (CUDA minor + Torch/Triton bumps). p95 generation latency jumped ~18% on small-batch flows and KV cache memory growth on long-chat tests :eyes:
sara: Ugh. Which merge specifically? CUDA driver or Triton change? :thinking:
michael: We pulled cuda 12.3.1 -> 12.3.3 and torch 2.2.1 -> 2.2.2, plus Triton 2.1.0 -> 2.1.1 in the same deploy window. CI showed a perf step in the runtime tests at 03:14 UTC (see CI run 2026-11-17_0314).
amy: Logs copied from the perf job: ```[perf-run] baseline p95=42ms -> head p95=50ms; avg tokens/sec -12%; kv-cache RSS after 10k steps: baseline 1.1GB -> head 1.6GB```
sara: Any kernel differences in the profile? Can we get nvprof/Traces?
nate: I uploaded a short perf trace to /tmp/kv-diff.trace. Quick diff shows some matmul kernels switched from fused_gemm_fp16 to triton_matmul_GF32 (names obfuscated), and a new attention kernel choosing a different algo for short sequence lengths. Also saw more fallback to generic softmax kernel with higher register pressure.
michael: That matches a theory: minor libcublas/cuDNN heuristics changed selection thresholds so our kernel selector picks different kernels for the 32/64 seq breakpoints. Could affect workspace and scheduling.
amy: Started a git-bisect across the infra merges. Early result: master@before-merge -> master@after-triton shows perf step. bisect log: ```good: 1804801120; bad: 1809002345; culprit-range: PR#4721 (triton runtime flags + kernel hints)```
sara: PR 4721? That was the small default-kernel-tuning and adds a new Triton operator hint flag. It was supposed to nudge kernels to fused path but maybe interacts with cudnn heuristics.
michael: Can you paste the failing CI job link? ci-bot: https://ci.internal/runs/2026/1809002345 - job shows p95 surge and one mem OOM transient on long-chat test.
nate: Quick repro command I ran locally: ```./tools/perf_runner --model=gpt-small --batch=1 --seq=128 --runs=1000 --enable-kv-cache``` baseline image vs head diff produced this snippet: ```2026-11-17T03:21:45Z INFO kernel: selected triton_matmul_v2 workspace=64MB time=0.86ms; baseline selected fused_gemm_v1 workspace=24MB time=0.58ms```
amy: So workspace up and slower. Also KV cache RSS climbs faster because of increased per-request scratch.
sara: Could be Triton change that enables larger workspace or a cuBLAS algo switch. Any transient warnings in dmesg or CUDA logs?
michael: I saw cudnn verbose show different algo chosen when seed workspace>32MB. Looks like cuda driver 12.3.3 prefers algos with higher scratch for these shapes.
nate: I ran the runtime with env override TRITON_FORCE_MATMUL=FUSED_GEMM_V1; locally latency returned to baseline and KV RSS stabilized. That suggests the new default path is the problem.
amy: Good find. Can we ship a temporary workaround: force the fused kernel selection for the affected model shapes until we sort upstream?
sara: Opswise, we should hold the Triton bump rollout for Dedicated fleets. For Hosted, we can gate by model or add a transient config flag.
michael: I started a minimal revert PR that flips the triton flag to previous default: PR#4753 (revert PR#4721 default hints). I also filed issue infra#998: "kernel selection regression after triton hint change + cuda 12.3.3" with traces.
nate: Plan: 1) revert default via PR#4753 (hold rollout) 2) land a runtime toggle so we can force old kernel selection per-model 3) add CI perf-check explicit for small-batch p95 and kv-rss regression on long chats 4) engage Triton maintainers if driver heuristics changed
amy: Could we add an adaptive batching tweak to avoid small-batch sensitivity? Maybe increase the batching window for the tiny flows to smooth out the algorithm choice noise.
michael: That's possible but it's a bigger change. Short term I'd prefer the revert + toggle. Long term add a test harness to exercise seq=32/64/128 boundaries in CI gating.
sara: Agree. Also tag security/regulatory folks since KV RSS growth might blow host mem limits under Dedicated customers.
deploy-bot: Held rollout of infra/2026-11-16 for all Dedicated pools as requested by eng-runtime. PR#4753 queued for review.
amy: I'll mark this as rollout-blocker on the release board and ping infra for expedited review. :thumbsup:
sara: Thanks team. Nate, can you drop the perf trace link into issue infra#998 and add the bisect commands you ran?
nate: Done — pasted trace, bisect steps, and repro commands in infra#998. Will keep monitoring. :eyes:
